First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y,$ treating $x$ and $z$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\frac{x}{z}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{z})\,dy\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[{\int }_{0}^{{z}^{2}}\frac{x}{z}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{z})\,dy]dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{[\frac{x}{z}\cdot z\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{z})]}_{y=0}^{y={z}^{2}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{z})]}_{y=0}^{y={z}^{2}}\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x(\operatorname{sin}⁡z-\operatorname{sin}⁡0)\,dz\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $z,$ treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz\,dx & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡z\,dz]dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[-x\operatorname{cos}⁡z]_{z=0}^{z=\pi /2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x(-0+1)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}x\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}x\,dx & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{x=-1}^{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(0-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
